criterion_notes.c1: Examines compound-level and household-level piped water and sewered sanitation service access, service disconnection and reconnection, working connection status, water consumption, water expenditure, and water-fetching time in informal settlements in Nairobi.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain reading, the study evaluates utility governance, customer engagement, and contract enforcement policies by Nairobi's municipal water and sanitation utility. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, while the first experimental arm (tenant face-to-face engagement) is behavioural/informational outreach, the second experimental arm directly tests a rule-type mechanism governing service access: systematic contract enforcement of utility disconnection rules for nonpayment of consumption bills and subsidized last-mile connection loans, governed by explicit arrears eligibility thresholds, formal disconnection notices, financial hardship exemptions/flexible payment plan accommodations, physical service disconnections, and discretionary reconnection without enforcing full-balance or reconnection-fee requirements.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical primary quantitative study implementing two randomized controlled field experiments (an individual-level RCT for tenant engagement and a two-stage street-cluster-randomized trial for disconnection contract enforcement) combined with five years of administrative utility billing data and primary surveys of property owners and tenants.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports multiple household and compound service access outcomes nine months post-intervention (Table 7 and Section 8.5), including actual utility disconnections and reconnections, having a piped water connection, having a pour-flush toilet connected in the compound, having a working piped water connection, using piped water to the compound as the main water source, metered piped water consumption, monthly household expenditure on water, and weekly time spent fetching water (alongside bill/loan repayment and rental outcomes). Per the A18 safeguard, null treatment effects on endline access do not affect eligibility.
criterion_notes.c5: Population, units of analysis (multi-household compounds, property owners, and tenant households), randomized exposures, access and payment outcomes, and experimental study designs are all clearly reported with sample sizes and statistical estimates.

evidence_quotes.quote: We estimate the impacts of two interventions implemented as field experiments in informal settlements by Nairobi’s water and sanitation utility to improve revenue collection efficiency and last mile connection loan repayment: (i) face-to-face engagement between utility staff and customers to encourage payment and (ii) contract enforcement for service disconnection due to nonpayment in the form of transparent and credible disconnection notices.

The second approach was to systematically enforce the terms of the contract that the property owners had signed with the utility, specifying service disconnection for property owners with signiﬁcant payment arrears.

Poster notiﬁcations included a contact number for property owners or tenants to contact the utility and dispute their balance or provide justiﬁcation for why they were unable to aﬀord to pay for the service and agree on a payment plan. If property owners were found to be indigent and/or agreed to a ﬂexible payment plan, they would not be disconnected.

This generated 147 distinct street clusters. We then randomized 73 clusters consisting of 1,584 accounts into the treatment group, while the remaining 74 clusters (1,669 accounts) were left as pure controls.

evidence_quotes.quote: The enforcement intervention had little eﬀect on compound connections to water and sanitation services. The majority of the 96 disconnected compounds were reconnected after agreeing to pay a portion of their balance.

raw_response.exposure: (1) Contract enforcement of utility disconnection rules for nonpayment of water/sewer bills and connection loans (targeted arrears threshold, five-step notice protocol, hardship exemption/payment-plan accommodation, physical disconnection, and flexible reconnection); and (2) face-to-face utility outreach engagement with tenants regarding compound bill arrears.
raw_response.outcome: Piped water connection status, working piped water connection status, pour-flush sewered toilet presence, main household water source, metered piped water consumption, household monthly water expenditure, weekly water-fetching time, physical disconnections and reconnections, utility bill/loan payment outcomes, perceptions of utility fairness/quality, and compound rental market outcomes.
raw_response.population_and_sample: Multi-household compounds, property owners, and tenant households connected to municipal piped water and sewer lines in informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya (5,091 surveyed property owners across 6 settlements; N = 2,584 compounds with tenants in the engagement RCT; 3,253 accounts across 147 street clusters in 4 settlements for the enforcement RCT, with N = 1,001 disconnection-eligible compounds in the primary ITT payment analysis and ~600 compounds in the 9-month follow-up property owner and tenant surveys).
raw_response.rationale: This NBER working paper meets all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. It reports two randomized field experiments in Nairobi's informal settlements, one of which directly evaluates systematic contract enforcement of utility service disconnection rules for arrears on water/sewer bills and subsidized connection loans—incorporating explicit arrears thresholds, formal notices, financial hardship exemptions/payment plans, physical disconnections, and flexible reconnection discretion—and measures nine-month impacts on compound piped water and sanitation connections, working connection status, primary water source, metered consumption, water expenditure, and fetching time (with quantitative estimates extractable for synthesis). Null treatment effects on endline water and sanitation access do not affect eligibility.
raw_response.study_design: Randomized controlled field experiments (individual-level RCT for tenant engagement and two-stage street-cluster-randomized controlled trial for contract enforcement of service disconnection) using utility administrative billing records and property owner/tenant surveys.
